pilot_attacks.key_finding: TapeStar is a merchant instrument sold openly (not captive): the differentiation must be restated to the delamination/lock-in-thermal channel, transport-Ic-calibrated acceptance reporting, cable/CICC stations, and neutral-referee positioning against a competitor that is itself a tape producer; TapeStar's actual capability gaps must be verified from its datasheet before P6.
pilot_attacks.kill_tests: Technical: blind-correlated <5% Ic prediction plus demonstrated delamination detection TapeStar lacks. Commercial: if tape vendors' TapeStar data is accepted by magnet builders as-is, the neutral-referee premium never materializes.

pilot_attacks.key_finding: Strongest counterargument is platform absorption: DG Matrix already sits inside NVIDIA's MGX reference architecture and every shelf vendor has in-house power electronics; the merchant case rests on protection being safety-critical, certification-heavy, and cross-vendor (SEL analogy). Certification timeline (UL/IEC for a novel 800V hybrid breaker shelf) is the second-order kill path.
pilot_attacks.kill_tests: Technical: <100us bidirectional clearing at 800V/500A with arc discrimination, no nuisance trips at 1MW-rack transient levels, 10,000 hot-swap cycles. Commercial: an OCP-published reference protection design shipped integrated by Delta/Vertiv before certification completes.

pilot_attacks.key_finding: Two stacked contingencies: the binding A/B existence proof (envelope protection must measurably reduce degradation) and a demand instrument that does not yet exist (lender/insurer LOI or OEM co-development). Hub demand is fact-supported at 5/7 restored (~$5B) but lender-requirement behavior is inference; hydrogen FID weakness is documented.
pilot_attacks.kill_tests: Technical: 2,000h A/B shows no statistically significant degradation-rate reduction. Commercial: financiers accept OEM warranties + plant DCS logs, refusing to price third-party evidence hardware.
